hero_subtitle: Gateway to the Sahara and Erg Chebbi dunes: camel treks, desert camps and Saharan horizons — Merzouga is the door between the Atlas and the dunes.

overview.title: Welcome to the Sahara Gateway
overview.p1: Merzouga sits on the edge of the majestic Erg Chebbi dunes. Kasbahs, desert tracks and starry horizons define the area. It is the ultimate base for Erg Chebbi, camel treks and overnight desert camps.
overview.p2: Two to three days cover the dunes, a camel trek and a night in camp — plus Khamlia, Dayet Srji or Rissani oasis if you stay longer. Use Merzouga as a highlight on a Moroccan desert circuit.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Merzouga
places.subtitle: Dunes, camel treks, camps and the stops that define the desert gateway.

erg.title: Erg Chebbi
erg.desc: Vast golden dunes rising above Merzouga — the heart of every Sahara visit here.

village.title: Merzouga Village
village.desc: Small desert gateway village with hotels, cafés and the trailhead to the erg.

camel.title: Camel Trek
camel.desc: Classic camel ride into the dunes at sunset or sunrise — the signature Merzouga experience.

camp.title: Desert Camp
camp.desc: Overnight in a Berber-style camp under the stars — dinner, drums and dune silence.

khamlia.title: Khamlia
khamlia.desc: Black desert village known for Gnawa music, tea and warm hospitality near the dunes.

dayet.title: Dayet Srji
dayet.desc: Seasonal lake at the foot of the dunes — flamingos when water is present after rains.

rissani.title: Rissani
rissani.desc: Historic market town and gateway — souk days, kasbahs and the Moulay Ali Cherif mausoleum.

hassilabied.title: Hassilabied
hassilabied.desc: Quiet village on the edge of the erg — hotels with dune views and a calmer base than central Merzouga.

fossils.title: Fossil Workshops
fossils.desc: Local workshops and shops selling trilobites and polished fossils from the Erfoud region.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Dunes, a night in camp, and the villages around Erg Chebbi.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Drive or walk to the edge of Erg Chebbi. Climb a dune for the first panoramic view before the heat peaks.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Return to the village for lunch, fossil shops, and time to arrange your camel trek and camp.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Watch sunset from a dune ridge, then dinner at your hotel or a village restaurant.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: A quiet morning in the village or Hassilabied; rest before the afternoon trek.
detailed_itinerary.day2_a: Afternoon — Camel trek into Erg Chebbi
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Depart as arranged with your camp: camel trek into the dunes toward your overnight stay.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Berber dinner, drums and stars; sleep in a tent or camp with optional sunrise climb.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Climb for sunrise, breakfast at camp, then camel or 4x4 back to the village.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Gnawa music and tea in Khamlia, or Rissani’s souk and Moulay Ali Cherif mausoleum.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Quiet dinner before onward travel toward Erfoud, Tinghir or Ouarzazate.

directory.title: Hotels, Kasbahs & Desert Camps in Merzouga
directory.subtitle: Filter by type and area — village edge, Hassilabied, or overnight in the dunes.

eat.title: Where to Eat in Merzouga
eat.subtitle: Tagines, grilled meats and mint tea — village restaurants and hotel tables with dune views.

dunes.title: Restaurant Les Dunes
dunes.desc: Classic tagines and grilled dishes with a terrace facing the erg — a reliable village favourite.

yasmina.title: Restaurant Yasmina
yasmina.desc: Hotel restaurant open to outside guests — Moroccan menus and views toward Erg Chebbi.

sud.title: Café du Sud
sud.desc: Simple café-restaurant for breakfast, omelettes, mint tea and a break from the heat.

mohayut.title: Kasbah Mohayut Restaurant
mohayut.desc: Moroccan set menus in a kasbah setting at the foot of the dunes — popular with overnight guests.

berbere.title: Restaurant Berbère
berbere.desc: Home-style Berber cooking in Hassilabied — couscous, tagine and a quieter evening than the main village strip.

camp.title: Dinner at Desert Camp
camp.desc: Most overnight camps include a Berber dinner under the stars — often the highlight of a Merzouga stay.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: The nearest airport is Errachidia (ERH), about a 2-hour drive away. 4x4 vehicles and private transfers are ideal for exploring the desert tracks around Merzouga.

bargain.title: Dress & Etiquette
bargain.desc: Wear light, breathable clothing during the day and pack warm layers for chilly desert nights. A scarf or head wrap is essential for protection against sand and sun.

water.title: Safety & Atmosphere
water.desc: Merzouga is very welcoming and safe for travellers. Always stay hydrated, drink bottled water, and book desert camps through trusted operators.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Merzouga
daytrips.subtitle: Easy excursions and desert routes that fit comfortably into a single day.

rabat.title: Erfoud & Draa Valley
rabat.desc: South into the Draa Valley — palm groves, kasbahs and the road toward the desert.

zagora.title: Erfoud
zagora.desc: Fossil capital and desert gateway, about 40 minutes north of Merzouga.

mohammedia.title: Dadès & Todra
mohammedia.desc: Gorges and valley scenery on the road west — often combined with a desert circuit.

azemmour.title: Marrakech (circuit)
azemmour.desc: Many travellers continue or return via the High Atlas Tizi n’Tichka pass to Marrakech.

q1.question: ¿Cuántos días pasar en Merzouga?
q1.answer: Dos días completos cubren los principales sitios con comodidad. Tres o cuatro días permiten un ritmo relajado más una excursión a Rissani o a los oasis cercanos.

q2.question: ¿Es segura Merzouga para turistas?
q2.answer: Sí. Merzouga es muy segura y acogedora. Reserve siempre campamentos y guías a través de operadores locales verificados.

q3.question: ¿Qué moneda y se puede pagar con tarjeta?
q3.answer: Marruecos usa el dírham (MAD). Las tarjetas se aceptan en hoteles grandes, pero lleve efectivo para tiendas pequeñas, propinas y mercados.

q4.question: ¿Cómo llegar a Merzouga desde el aeropuerto más cercano?
q4.answer: El aeropuerto más cercano es Errachidia (ERH), a unas 2 horas en coche. Traslados privados, taxis o alquiler de coches están fácilmente disponibles.
